Use one of the recommended methods below. For more installation options, uninstall steps, and troubleshooting, see the [setup documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup). 1. Install Claude Code: **MacOS/Linux (Recommended):** ```bash curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash ``` **Homebrew (MacOS/Linux):** ```bash brew install --cask claude-code ``` **Windows (Recommended):** ```powershell irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex ``` **WinGet (Windows):** ```powershell winget install Anthropic.ClaudeCode ``` **NPM (Deprecated):** ```bash npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code ``` 2. Navigate to your project directory and run `claude`. ## Plugins Anthropic's Claude Code plugins are developed in [claude-plugins-official](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official). See the [plugins directory](./plugins/README.md) for more about plugins. ## Reporting Bugs We welcome your feedback. Use the `/bug` command to report issues directly within Claude Code, or file a [GitHub issue](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues). ## Connect on Discord Join the [Claude Developers Discord](https://anthropic.com/discord) to connect with other developers using Claude Code. Get help, share feedback, and discuss your projects with the community. ## Data collection, usage, and retention When you use Claude Code, we collect feedback, which includes usage data (such as code acceptance or rejections), associated conversation data, and user feedback submitted via the `/bug` command. ### How we use your data See our [data usage policies](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage). ### Privacy safeguards We have implemented several safeguards to protect your data, including limited retention periods for sensitive information, restricted access to user session data, and clear policies against using feedback for model training. readmeHtml:
Claude Code

Claude Code is an agentic coding tool that lives in your terminal, understands your codebase, and helps you code faster by executing routine tasks, explaining complex code, and handling git workflows -- all through natural language commands. Use it in your terminal, IDE, or tag @claude on Github.

Learn more in the official documentation.

Get started

Note

Installation via npm is deprecated. Use one of the recommended methods below.

For more installation options, uninstall steps, and troubleshooting, see the setup documentation.

  1. Install Claude Code:

    MacOS/Linux (Recommended):

    curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash

    Homebrew (MacOS/Linux):

    brew install --cask claude-code

    Windows (Recommended):

    irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex

    WinGet (Windows):

    winget install Anthropic.ClaudeCode

    NPM (Deprecated):

    npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code

  2. Navigate to your project directory and run claude.

Plugins

Anthropic's Claude Code plugins are developed in claude-plugins-official. See the plugins directory for more about plugins.

Reporting Bugs

We welcome your feedback. Use the /bug command to report issues directly within Claude Code, or file a GitHub issue.

Connect on Discord

Join the Claude Developers Discord to connect with other developers using Claude Code. Get help, share feedback, and discuss your projects with the community.

Data collection, usage, and retention

When you use Claude Code, we collect feedback, which includes usage data (such as code acceptance or rejections), associated conversation data, and user feedback submitted via the /bug command.

How we use your data

See our data usage policies.

Privacy safeguards

We have implemented several safeguards to protect your data, including limited retention periods for sensitive information, restricted access to user session data, and clear policies against using feedback for model training.

For full details, please review our Commercial Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.

releases.name: v2.1.327
releases.body:
## What's changed

- Added a confirmation before `/install-github-app` changes a repository
- Added `claude mcp add-json <name> -` to read the server's JSON from stdin, so tokens can stay off the command line; not available inside a Claude Code session
- Added a line when a resumed session's earlier messages can't be loaded
- Added a list in `/status` of broken agent, skill, command and output style files, keybinding errors, an unavailable sandbox, ignored permission settings and hook matchers that never match
- Added a note in `/config` when other settings override a row
- Added `x-claude-code-managed-settings-checksum` to the gateway hint headers; sent where managed settings set `CLAUDE_CODE_GATEWAY_HINT_HEADERS=1`, including where they already do
- Added support for naming a session's billing group with the `attributionProject` setting, for Claude apps gateways that set `admin.billing_group_tag`
- Added `/tui classic` as the name for the non-fullscreen renderer; `/tui default` still works
- Remote Control: Fixed stopping the server in worktree mode deleting a running session's git-ignored files, such as `.env`
- Fixed self-hosted runners with `--use-anthropic-git-proxy` deleting

releases.name: v2.1.326
releases.body:
## What's changed

- Added support for turning on Code Mode while agent teams are enabled; if you already turned it on, sessions with teams on now start in Code Mode
- Added a startup warning when an `--allowedTools`, `--disallowedTools` or `--tools` value has an entry that doesn't look like a complete rule
- Added a message explaining why MCP servers stop loading when an administrator adds `managed-mcp.json` during a session
- Added a row to `/status` that says when your provider or an environment variable such as `DISABLE_TELEMETRY` turns features off
- Added a note in `/plugin` and `claude plugin list` when a malformed `plugin.json` field such as `author` or `homepage` is ignored
- Added Ctrl+O to show hidden startup notices
- Added a hint in the empty prompt that says what to do after a request fails
- Added an `esc to stop` footer hint in a subagent's view where Esc would stop it
- Added `OTEL_RESOURCE_INCLUDE_HOST` to include `host.name` and `host.id` in OpenTelemetry resource attributes (off by default)
- Added `overflowX="scroll"` on a mod's `Box`, and `maxLines` and `wrap="clip"` on its `Text`
- Fixed `cp` of a file being refused when only its source was covered by an `Edi

releases.name: v2.1.325
releases.body:
## What's changed

- Fixed a security issue in how zstd-compressed responses are decoded
- Added a spinner tip in VS Code and similar integrated terminals about re-running a notebook cell, shown once Claude has read or edited a Jupyter notebook
- Added a line under the error shown when your organization's policy blocks a request, saying how to continue: run `/rewind` and change the message, or run `/clear`
- Added a note for Claude when a sandboxed `git checkout`, `git stash` or autostash pull cannot update protected files such as those in `.claude`
- Fixed `/security-review` and skills' inline git commands stopping with an error in worktrees of bare repositories, `--separate-git-dir` checkouts and Android `repo` checkouts
- Fixed subagents with their own model being moved to the plan-mode model when the model setting is `opusplan` or `haiku`
- Fixed subagents on a different model sizing file reads and MCP results with the main session's model
- Fixed sessions on many third-party gateways and Foundry stopping with a context length error on every turn instead of compacting
- Fixed recent turns sometimes going missing from a resumed session after Claude Code stopped without a clean e

releases.name: v2.1.323
releases.body:
## What's changed

- Added Code Mode, an experimental opt-in in which Claude writes JavaScript to call its tools; see https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-mode to turn it on, or to turn it off for an organization
- Added `engines["claude-code"]` to `plugin.json`: plugins outside their stated Claude Code version range are not installed, updated or loaded, and install and update pick the newest version that fits
- Added type checking of a plugin's TypeScript hooks module to `claude plugin validate`; each finding is a warning, and `--strict` fails on it
- Added to `claude plugin validate` the `$` nouns a mod's `engine.create` hook adds, withholds or replaces
- Added support for `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_MODEL` in managed settings for Claude Desktop sessions on third-party providers (takes effect once Claude Desktop includes this version)
- Added an options menu (stop, switch to usage credits, upgrade) when a model needs usage credits that are turned off or used up
- Added a progress heartbeat every 30 seconds while hooks run long in `claude -p` and SDK sessions, so a host such as Claude Desktop won't end the turn as hung (once it includes this version)
- Added `.docx` support to Artifact

releases.name: v2.1.322
releases.body:
## What's changed

- Added fast mode on Vertex in the global, us and eu regions, falling back to standard speed if Vertex refuses it

aiSummary.oneLiner: An official, terminal-based AI coding assistant powered directly by the Claude model family.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Claude Code is a command-line interface tool developed by Anthropic that deeply integrates their Claude AI models directly into a developer's local environment. It is designed to understand entire codebases by autonomously navigating directories, reading files, and executing local shell commands for context. The tool assists with complex refactoring, bug hunting, and feature implementation without requiring developers to leave their terminal or copy-paste code into a browser. It maintains a secure, local execution perimeter while leveraging the advanced reasoning capabilities of models like Claude 3.5 Sonnet. This drastically reduces context switching and accelerates the software development lifecycle.
keyFeatures: Native terminal integration: Operates entirely within the command line, integrating seamlessly into existing shell environments and workflows.
Autonomous codebase navigation: Capable of searching directories, reading files, and grepping for specific patterns to build context automatically.
Local command execution: Safely runs local tests, linters, and build scripts to verify code changes before finalizing them.
Advanced model reasoning: Powered directly by Anthropic's most capable models, ensuring high-quality architectural advice and code generation.
Context-aware refactoring: Understands the broader repository structure, allowing it to safely execute multi-file changes and updates.

useCases.title: Automated Bug Resolution
useCases.description: Instruct the assistant to locate the source of a specific error trace, write the fix, and run the test suite to verify it.

useCases.title: Complex Code Refactoring
useCases.description: Command the tool to migrate an entire directory of components to a new framework API across multiple interdependent files.

useCases.title: Codebase Onboarding
useCases.description: Ask the terminal assistant to explain the architecture and data flow of a massive, unfamiliar repository dynamically.

useCases.title: Rapid Feature Implementation
useCases.description: Describe a new feature in natural language and allow the tool to scaffold the necessary files, logic, and tests automatically.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Professional software engineers and developers who prefer working in terminal environments and want powerful, context-aware AI assistance. It requires familiarity with command-line interfaces and local development workflows.
